title: Generalized Spin Groups and Applications to Magnons
authors: Xinhai Tu, Di Wang, Yuxuan Mu, Xiangang Wan
abstract: Spin groups provide the natural symmetry framework for the isotropic Heisenberg model, in which spin and lattice degrees of freedom are separable. They have recently found broad applications in describing electronic band structure, magnon band topology, and transport phenomena. However, a typical spin Hamiltonian describing magnons contains not only isotropic Heisenberg exchange but also anisotropic interactions induced by spin-orbit coupling (SOC), including the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction, the Gamma exchange, and the single-ion anisotropy (SIA), which strongly influence magnon properties. More recently, some studies have also revealed relativistic magnon transport phenomena in altermagnets. Such systems typically exhibit partial spin-lattice locking, but are commonly assumed to be described by conventional magnetic groups. Here, we develop a systematic symmetry framework, generalized spin groups, for magnons. We first classify the symmetries of Heisenberg, DM, Gamma, and SIA interactions. The resulting classification contains 6 spin-only groups, together with a total of 161 nontrivial spin groups. The symmetries of magnetically ordered phases are then obtained through spontaneous symmetry breaking of the corresponding parent groups for spin Hamiltonians. We also identify 6 spin-only groups for ordered states, which generate 90, 264, 157, 264, 387, and 598 nontrivial spin groups, respectively. Finally, we apply generalized spin groups to the magnon thermal conductivity and spin conductivity tensors and derive all the symmetry-allowed forms. Our results provide a unified symmetry framework for analyzing magnon transport both with and without SOC, yielding more refined constraints on magnon responses.
summary: This paper introduces Generalized Spin Groups (GSGs) to provide a comprehensive symmetry framework for analyzing magnons in magnetic materials, particularly when Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) is present. By classifying symmetries beyond simple isotropic models, the authors derive strict constraints on magnon transport properties like thermal and spin conductivity tensors. This unified approach significantly refines the theoretical understanding of magnon behavior in complex magnetic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a systematic symmetry framework for magnons that accurately describes systems beyond the simple isotropic Heisenberg model, especially when Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) introduces complex anisotropic interactions.
main_result: The authors develop Generalized Spin Groups (GSGs), classifying symmetries into 6 spin-only groups and yielding a total of 161 nontrivial spin groups, providing a unified analysis for magnon transport with or without SOC.
method: The methodology involves classifying symmetries of spin Hamiltonians (including Heisenberg, DM, $\Gamma$, and SIA terms) by decomposing the symmetry group into a Spin-Only Group (SOG) and a Non-trivial Spin Group (NSG).
model_or_system: The study focuses on magnon excitations in magnetic materials described by spin Hamiltonians, utilizing examples like the MnPS3 model. The Hamiltonian incorporates isotropic exchange, DM, $\Gamma$ exchange, and SIA terms.
key_observables: Magnon thermal conductivity and spin conductivity tensors, and the classification of symmetry-allowed magnon transport channels.
important_parameters: The presence and type of anisotropic interactions induced by SOC (DM, $\Gamma$, SIA) are critical parameters determining the symmetry group.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the residual symmetries can be systematically captured by the GSG structure, moving beyond the limitations of conventional magnetic groups which assume full spin-lattice locking.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the symmetry progression from no SOC to full spin-lattice locking. Tables I, II, and S1-S3 summarize the classification of SOGs and NSGs for various interactions and magnetic configurations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the GSG framework by first classifying symmetries for individual interactions (Heisenberg, DM, etc.), then determining symmetries for ordered states via spontaneous symmetry breaking, and finally applying the resulting symmetry constraints to derive allowed forms for magnon transport tensors.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the rigorous group-theoretic approach to constraining physical responses (like transport tensors) based on underlying symmetries is highly relevant to developing symmetry-protected topological phases or understanding quantum constraints in many-body systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic progression from independent to fully locked spin and lattice operations. (a) In the absence of SOC, spin operations of spin Hamiltonian act independently of lattice operations , and the symmetry of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian is described by ZS 2 ⊗SO(3)S ⊗CL. (b) With DM interaction, residual spin-only operations coexist with combined spin-lattice operations. This partially locked spin Hamiltonian can be described by GSGs. (c) In the limiting case of complete spin-lattice locking, spin operations are tied to lattice operations, and the symmetry of the spin Hamiltonian has symmetry ZS 2 ⊗CS·L.
